name: Bu (Zaranda)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.quote: Bu: has two tones. Only Hi (á) and contour (â, ǎ) tones will be noted. Lo tones will remain unmarked (a).
new_statements.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2008. Bu:, aka Zaranda (Chadic, South-Bauchi West): Wordlist and grammatical notes. In Gábor Takács (ed.), Semito-Hamitic Festschrift for A.B. Dolgopolsky and H. Jungraithmayr, 93-119. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. HAL preprint halshs-00644360.
new_statements.locator: §1 Phonology, 'Tones', HAL preprint p. 1 (PDF p. 2; the opening page of the printed article, pp. 93-94)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bu (Zaranda) is described as a two-tone language (High vs Low, with falling and rising contours on single syllables); the sketch says nothing at all about word stress or accent, and no other source on the language does either. Tone is lexical and grammatical (floating Hi of DO clitics, tonal TAM marking, Low-tone verbal plural), with depressor-type blocking by non-implosive voiced obstruents.
new_statements.exceptions: Not applicable; the only prosodic remarks concern tone: floating Hi tone after singular Direct-Object clitics is blocked when the following word begins with a non-implosive voiced obstruent (p. 2), and genitive clitic tones vary with the preceding syllable.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical/grammatical tone marked on words in the wordlist and on clitics in phrases; no statement about stress at word or phrase level, and no instrumental data. Based on eight days of elicitation (Jan. and Nov. 2002) with the few remaining speakers at Zaranda Haɓe.
new_statements.identity_note: The source describes Bu:/Bùù as spoken at Zaranda Haɓe (9.57E, 10.28N), the old hill village, by 'a few hundred' remaining speakers; the new Zaranda village has shifted to Hausa/Fulfulde. Caron treats Bu as a distinct language within the Geji cluster (no intercomprehension with Bolu, Pelu, Geji), matching Glottolog zara1252 / ISO zbu. Ethnologue earlier lumped it under Geji (gji), which Caron 2008 fn. 1 rejects. Not a differently named variety.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2008. Bu:, aka Zaranda (Chadic, South-Bauchi West): Wordlist and grammatical notes. In Gábor Takács (ed.), Semito-Hamitic Festschrift for A.B. Dolgopolsky and H. Jungraithmayr, 93-119. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. HAL preprint halshs-00644360.

sources.locator: §1 Phonology, 'Tones', HAL preprint p. 1 (PDF p. 2; the opening page of the printed article, pp. 93-94)
sources.note: §1 Phonology (preprint p. 1 = PDF p. 2) gives consonants, vowels and a three-line 'Tones' paragraph: two tones (Hi vs unmarked Lo, plus falling and rising contours). The words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur anywhere in the 38-page preprint (grammatical notes + wordlist); no statement about word stress.

sources.citation: Newman, Paul. 2022. A Chadic bibliography, 5th ed. (online).
sources.note: Used as an index: the only item keyed [Zaranda] is Caron 2008a ('Includes extensive wordlist'); Shimizu 1978b is keyed [South-Bauchi]. No other Zaranda-specific description is listed.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page zara1252 (Bu, Nigeria) and HAL API search q=Zaranda.
sources.note: Glottolog cites Shimizu 1978, Caron 2009 pp. 640-641 (Les Zaar et leurs voisins), Caron 2011 (Les langues tchadiques) and Ethnologue; HAL returns only Caron 2008 for Zaranda plus the SBW-wide papers fetched sources above. Caron 2013 'Tonal inversion in Geji and Pelu' (halshs-01487220) has no deposited file.

sources.note: Entry 'Buu / 1.A Zaranda 1.B Bùù... 4. 750 (LA 1971), a few hundred (Caron 2002)... Grammar: Caron (2008); Ethnographic: Gunn (1953)'; classified in the Geji cluster. No phonological information.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2014. Number in South-Bauchi West languages (Chadic, Nigeria). HAL halshs-00922755 (preprint of a chapter).
sources.note: Morphosyntax of number; Zaranda cited for 2pl verbal plural. No stress or tone-system statement.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2012. Loanwords in South-Bauchi-West Chadic languages. Paper, Naples, Sept. 2012 (with annex).
sources.note: No stress. Records that Caron holds c. 1,000 Zaranda lexical items in a Toolbox database and that his published Zaranda data are in RefLex; Kraft 1981 does not cover Zaranda.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2011. Comment se sortir d'un mauvais pas: variation sur la 2ème personne dans les langues tchadiques du groupe sud-Bauchi occidental (SBW). HAL.
sources.note: Zaranda 2nd-person pronoun/verbal-plural morphology, including a Low-tone verbal plural mark. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2009. Documenting linguistic varieties of the South-Bauchi group (project description, HAL).
sources.note: Lists Zaranda as a documented idiom of the Geji branch and describes its sociolinguistic situation (old hill village vs. new village shifted to Hausa). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2006. South-Bauchi West Pronominal and TAM Systems. In Bernard Caron & Petr Zima (eds.), Sprachbund in the West African Sahel, 93-112. Leuven: Peeters. HAL halshs-00644372.
sources.note: Preprint p. 3: 'Zaar and Gùùs have three tone levels, the others only two' (Bùù = Zaranda is the Geji-cluster language sampled, p. 3); fn. 3 (p. 5): 'Zaar and Gùùs (Sigidi) have 3 tone levels; the other languages have 2. Hi is marked with an acute accent; Lo with a grave; Mid is left unmarked.' Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2003. South-Bauchi West TAM System. Paper, 17th International Congress of Linguists (CIL 17), Prague, 24-29 July 2003. HAL halshs-00645356.
sources.note: p. 2 and fn. 2: same two-tone statement for the non-Zaar/Gùùs SBW languages (Bùù among them); 'accent' occurs only as the name of the tone diacritics. Nothing on stress.
